A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Standardised lung cancer pathway with booked slots. A lung cancer pathway on the Danish/Swedish/Norwegian model: fixed referral criteria, pre-booked CT, PET-CT, bronchoscopy and MDT slots, a named pathway owner, and published time limits for each step.
supported_en: Filha (May 2026) announces a national guideline with a standard referral, a common pathway and target times. Scientific Reports (2023) shows only 30% of Swedish lung pathway patients met the 30–44 day limit.
not_supported_en: No page we read measures the days a pathway saves, so the assumed 14 days (range 5–23) is not shown, and no page shows HUS has booked slots or a named pathway owner.

summary_en: In May 2026, the national lung cancer programme group published a guideline on diagnosing lung cancer (announced by Filha). It sets a standard referral to hospital, a common care pathway and target times for starting treatment. Neither the HUS pathway pages nor the LUVN pages we read show that HUS or LUVN applies these. On HUS's own pages, tests are planned case by case after the referral arrives, and tissue sample results usually take 2–3 weeks. For the effect, Scientific Reports (2023) shows Sweden's lung pathway time limit is 30–44 days, but only 30% of patients met it.
unanswered_en: We found no HUS or LUVN page on putting the 2026 national guideline into practice, booked slots or time limits for each step, and no study that measures days saved.
